To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
VPS13 is a lipid transporter that tethers the ER to mitochondria, late endosomes/lysosomes, and lipid droplets.
VPS13A, VPS13C, and VPS13D are lipid transport proteins localized at ER contact points that are involved in lipid transport between the ER and late endosomes/lysosomes and lipid droplets.
VPS13 is a lipid transport protein that can transport glycerol lipids between membranes and that VPS13 proteins bind to different organelles and tether them to the ER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the lipid transport protein VPS13 and its role in human neurological diseases.
the identification and characterization of proteins that are involved in the maintenance of cellular lipid homeostasis.
the role of VPS13 proteins in lipid transport between membranes and their role in human diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Vps13 and its homologs are lipid transport proteins that mediate the transport of phospholipids and other lipids between membranes.
the N-terminal region of VPS13 proteins has a hydrophobic channel with the ability to solubilize lipids and transport them to other organelles.
Vps13 proteins are lipid transporters between the ER and mitochondria, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and autophagosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

VPS13 is a membrane-bound lipid transporter that is localized to ER contact sites with other organelles and that mutations in VPS13 cause neurodegenerative diseases by disrupting the lipid homeostasis between these organelles.

Vps13 proteins are lipid transporters, and that they may be involved in the pathogenesis of chorea acanthocythosis and Parkinson’s disease.
